# This Bluetooth tracker uses LoRa mesh networks to find things - and I couldn't believe the accuracy
Follow ZDNET: Add us as a preferred source on Google. I've said it before, and I'll say it again: were a total game-changer for me. Being able to pinpoint and locate things like keys and wallets, wherever they are in the world, has saved me no end of heartache, headaches, and wasted time. And the proliferation of third-party tags means there are tags for all sorts of applications. Also: I hid 4 Bluetooth trackers (including AirTags) to test their reliability - here's how Android rivals comparedBut the one drawback is that all the tags rely on cellular and Wi-Fi networks. What if you could get tags that operated on their own networks and could operate independently of the networks built by multibillion-dollar corporations? That's exactly what the offers. OK, how does this work? And with most things, there are a lot of things I like about the T1000-E, and a few things I don't. But before I go any further, let me warn you that this card could very well be a gateway drug that pulls you into the huge world of LoRa mesh. LoRa stands for Long Range Radio and is a long-range wireless radio protocol that can be used to create a mesh. Also: I found an AirTag alternative that's twice as durable and works with Android phonesWhat's a mesh? It's an open-source, off-grid, decentralized mesh network designed to run on small, low-power devices. It doesn't need cell towers or the internet. It's a completely stand-alone, peer-to-peer radio system. If you're a bit like me and love getting your teeth into weird things, you'll soon be hip-deep in mesh transceivers and setting up . Why? Because you can.Note: Make sure you get the T1000-E, and not the or B variants. Only the E is designed to work with peer-to-peer mesh, and the A and B variants make use of and require their own network gateways. OK, back to the T1000-E. This is a card-sized tracker much like all the others. It's credit card-sized and as thick as a bunch of cards. Inside is a 700 mAh battery that's enough to power the card for a couple of days, along with all the tech wizardry for communication and location magic. Also: I put away my AirTag just minutes after trying this Bluetooth tracker alternative - here's whyThere's a super-loud buzzer, an LED status light, and a button to turn the unit on and off and control things like Bluetooth. Built for the apocalypse The shell is IP65-rated for dust and water intrusion, so it's fine to be out and about in the great outdoors. I like this a lot, but to achieve this level of dust and waterproofing, the manufacturer has opted for a magnetic charging pad on the back that uses pogo pins. Not only does this mean that you need a proprietary cable every time you need to charge the device, but the design means that if you try to charge the card while on the move (by, say, using a ), there's a good chance that it'll come loose and stop charging. I've come up with solutions using elastic bands or hot glue, but I wish there were a better way to keep the connector attached. It's a great tracker By default, you'll need to download the SenseCraft app ( / ) to set up and control the T1000-E. The app is OK, but not great. The instructions can be a bit vague; sometimes you'll stumble across sections in Chinese, and it's also trying to sell you more stuff (something I hate in an app for a product I've bought). My advice is that if you get stuck, hit the extensive support documentation wiki (complete with videos), or head over to the excellent r/meshtastic over on Reddit. Also: I took apart the new AirTag 2 and found a serious flaw in Apple's popular trackerIf you just want to use the tracker as a tracker, you've pretty much done everything you need to do. The app has a map that shows you the card's location, or you can use it to beacon your position to others when out and about by sharing your location. The card will use Bluetooth to connect to the app on the smartphone, but it can also connect to LoRaWAN, Meshtastic, Amazon Sidewalk, and Helium networks. Also: My new favorite AirTag alternative fits perfectly in my wallet - and is seriously durableIf you live in an area where there are people using mesh, that's going to be a great option that just works. You might decide to put nodes up for you to use around your home or work, extending the mesh for everyone. I found that Amazon Sidewalk was also a really good, workable option, especially in built-up areas. After all, there are a lot of and out there, so there's a pretty big mesh you can leverage. Loads of options. And yes, this could work in those apocalyptic scenarios where the power goes down, the cellular grids go quiet, and the zombies start to shuffle about. I've carried it in a pocket, bag, and strapped to the outside of my rucksack, and the GPS receiver is excellent even under subpar conditions. There's a lanyard slot on the card for attaching it to things. But there's more ... a lot more! But there's a lot more to the T1000-E. It's a lot more than a tracker card. It's a fully functional mesh transmitter that can be used to send and receive messages between other devices. If you want to get into this, then you'll need another mesh device (say, another tracker or a ). And this is where you start the slide into mesh obsession. Also: I slipped this stealthy $15 tracker into my favorite jacket - now it's an everyday essentialYou can also delve deeper into the card. For example, you can dump the firmware that Seeed Studio loaded onto the T1000-E, and install stock Meshtastic firmware onto it using the online flasher tool. Now you can use the Meshtastic app ( / ) to control the card, and I found this to be a whole lot better, especially if you want to go deeper into the card's capabilities. This is well beyond what I can go into here, but if you want something to get you started, this video will probably kick-start your obsession. ZDNET's buying advice The will set you back around $50. You'll sometimes see it for a lot more, but avoid those. Usually, if you wait a day or so, the prices will come down. Also: These are the closest things to AirTags for Android users (and better in some ways)For a pure tracker card, that's a pretty hefty price tag, but once you realize it can also serve as a messaging client and you can use it to send and receive messages for free, it starts to feel more reasonable. Mesh is great for off-grid comms and also for places like cruise ships, where the company will charge you an arm and a leg for Wi-Fi.

# 這款藍牙追蹤器用 LoRa Mesh 找東西，精準度讓我難以置信

我以前說過，現在還是要再說一次：這類追蹤標籤對我來說真的徹底改變了使用體驗。能夠在世界各地精準定位鑰匙、錢包這類物品，替我省下了無數心痛、頭痛和浪費掉的時間。第三方標籤越來越多，也代表現在已經有適合各種用途的追蹤標籤。

但這些標籤有一個缺點：它們都仰賴行動網路和 Wi-Fi 網路。如果有一種追蹤標籤，可以在自己的網路上運作，不必依靠那些由市值數十億美元企業建起來的網路呢？這正是這款產品提供的能力。

好，那它到底怎麼運作？和多數產品一樣，T1000-E 有很多我喜歡的地方，也有幾點我不喜歡。不過在繼續往下講之前，我得先提醒你，這張卡很可能會成為讓你跌進 LoRa Mesh 廣大世界的入門毒物。LoRa 是 Long Range Radio 的縮寫，是一種長距離無線電協定，可以用來建立 Mesh 網狀網路。

什麼是 Mesh？它是一種開源、離網、去中心化的網狀網路，設計用來在小型、低功耗裝置上運作。它不需要基地台，也不需要網際網路。這是一套完全獨立、點對點的無線電系統。如果你有點像我，喜歡鑽研奇奇怪怪的東西，很快就會深陷各種 Mesh 收發器，開始架設自己的節點。為什麼？因為你可以。

注意：請確認你買的是 T1000-E，而不是 A 或 B 版本。只有 E 版是設計來搭配點對點 Mesh 使用；A 版和 B 版則會使用、也需要各自的網路閘道器。

回到 T1000-E。這是一張卡片大小的追蹤器，和其他同類產品差不多。它的大小像信用卡，厚度則約等於一疊卡片。裡面有一顆 700 mAh 電池，足以讓這張卡運作幾天；另外也塞進了所有用於通訊與定位的技術元件。

它有一個音量很大的蜂鳴器、一盞 LED 狀態燈，以及一顆按鈕，可用來開關裝置，並控制藍牙等功能。

## 為末日情境打造

外殼具備 IP65 防塵防水等級，所以帶到戶外使用沒有問題。我很喜歡這點，但為了達到這樣的防塵防水能力，製造商選擇在背面採用磁吸充電板，並透過 pogo pin 彈簧針接點充電。

這不只代表每次充電都需要專用線材，也代表如果你想在移動中替這張卡充電，例如用某種行動電源之類的裝置，它很可能會鬆脫，然後停止充電。我自己想過用橡皮筋或熱熔膠來解決，但我還是希望有更好的方式，能讓接頭穩穩固定住。

## 它是很棒的追蹤器

預設情況下，你需要下載 SenseCraft app 來設定與控制 T1000-E。這個 app 還可以，但稱不上出色。說明有時候有點模糊；偶爾你會看到中文段落，而且它還會試圖向你推銷更多東西。對一個我已經買下來的產品來說，我很討厭 app 裡還出現這種推銷。

我的建議是，如果你卡住了，可以去看內容完整的支援文件 wiki，裡面也有影片；或者到 Reddit 上很棒的 r/meshtastic 社群看看。

如果你只是想把它當作追蹤器使用，那你基本上已經完成所有需要做的事了。app 裡有地圖，可以顯示這張卡的位置；你也可以在外出時透過分享位置，把自己的所在位置廣播給其他人。

這張卡會透過藍牙連接智慧型手機上的 app，但它也能連上 LoRaWAN、Meshtastic、Amazon Sidewalk 和 Helium 網路。

如果你住的地方有人在使用 Mesh，那會是一個很好、而且能直接運作的選項。你也可以選擇在住家或工作場所周圍架設節點，讓自己使用，同時也為所有人擴展 Mesh 覆蓋範圍。

我發現 Amazon Sidewalk 也是一個非常好用、可行的選項，尤其是在建成區。畢竟外面有很多相關裝置，所以你可以利用的 Mesh 規模其實相當大。選項很多。

沒錯，這也可以在那些末日情境中派上用場：停電、行動網路沉寂，殭屍開始在外面晃來晃去的時候。我把它放在口袋、包包裡，也曾綁在背包外側；即使在條件不太理想的情況下，GPS 接收器的表現仍然很出色。卡片上也有吊繩孔，方便把它固定在物品上。

## 但還有更多……多很多！

T1000-E 的能耐還不只這樣。它遠遠不只是一張追蹤卡。它是一個功能完整的 Mesh 發射器，可以在其他裝置之間收發訊息。如果你想深入玩這件事，就會需要另一台 Mesh 裝置，例如另一個追蹤器，或其他相容裝置。也就是從這裡開始，你會一路滑進對 Mesh 著迷的坑裡。

你也可以更深入地研究這張卡。例如，你可以把 Seeed Studio 載入 T1000-E 的韌體清掉，並使用線上燒錄工具把原版 Meshtastic 韌體安裝進去。這樣一來，你就可以用 Meshtastic app 控制這張卡；我發現這樣好用得多，尤其是當你想更深入探索這張卡的能力時。

這已經超出本文能詳細說明的範圍，但如果你想找個起點，原文提到的那支影片大概會讓你正式入坑。

## ZDNET 的購買建議

這款產品大約要價 50 美元。你有時候會看到它賣得貴很多，但請避開那些價格。通常只要等個一天左右，價格就會降下來。

如果只把它當成純粹的追蹤卡，這個價格相當不便宜；但當你意識到它也能作為訊息用戶端，並且可以免費收發訊息時，這個價格就開始顯得合理一些。

Mesh 很適合離網通訊，也很適合郵輪這類地方，因為船公司通常會把 Wi-Fi 收費訂得非常昂貴。
